answer: To mint an identity, an agent must stake 1,000 units behind a time-lock that doubles for every additional alias, hardening like quartz with each epoch; a farm running fifty fakes binds over sixty thousand units in capital alone. The engine verifies each bond on its epoch terrace before countersigning, releasing funds only after twenty clean rounds. Under a rising tide of clones, honest identities stay cheap while sybil farms price themselves out.
